quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: No, it is weaker than the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake, but it is safe if you use it correctly.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. Pick a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to stop a friend from driving drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Good ways to prevent drunk driving are: arrange an alternative ride home, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, keep them from leaving, and ask friends to help apply pressure.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: Something that damages the engine and should be avoided.
An effect similar to using the brakes.
Something that makes a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effect similar to using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a position that fits your riding conditions.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar during acceleration?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is speeding up faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. When you accelerate, the sidecar's weight makes it feel like it is falling behind.

questions.question: Where is the horn button located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The horn button is on the left handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Why should you NOT ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
The vehicle might block your escape route.
The driver may think you are trying to race them.
The driver may not see you and change lanes into you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may think you are trying to race them.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you and move into your lane. The vehicle may also block your escape route from other hazards.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea is NOT good?

options.text: Plan travel based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks to reach your destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan ride length based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader. Ride in a staggered formation for safety.

questions.question: You may not need extra space between you and the car ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see around the vehicle ahead.
The weather is good and traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather is good and traffic is light.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and the car ahead in bad conditions. Keep extra distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If you refuse a breath test when stopped by an officer:

options.text: The officer must let you go.
The officer cannot use what they saw in court.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: Maine has an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a breath test if an officer asks. If you refuse, your license will be suspended right away for up to six years.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is used for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limits.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of these matter except:
questions.correctAnswerText: It looks good.
questions.explanation: Pick a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around with no damage like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: The best way to ride in a group is generally in:
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Move into a single line when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: New riders in a group should ride:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: New riders should ride right behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind and lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: The best way to stop is to:

options.text: Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
Press the rear brake harder and harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: To stop in a straight line, apply both brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, use more front brake and less rear brake. Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead to stay straight.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to adjust to right away.
Make cars look closer than they are.
Show a narrow view behind you.
Make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show more of the road behind you than flat mirrors. But they make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances with curved mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have been riding that specific motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When stopped, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Keep first gear engaged while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Uses some rear braking when you apply the front brake.
Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
Brakes both front and rear equally when either brake is applied.
Learns and saves how hard you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system is a type of linked braking system. When you use the rear brake, some front braking power is also applied. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from coming back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest way is to:

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to simply go straight in your lane when crossing angled tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle is dangerous because it could send you into another lane.

questions.question: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are what type of sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about hazards or road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When road conditions require longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a larger distance behind other vehicles if your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see clearly, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of lanes. When wet, this oily strip is slippery. You can usually ride to the side of this strip and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To be more visible at intersections, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Reduce your distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and position your motorcycle where other drivers can see you. Maintain safe space between you and other vehicles. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: If rain starts while you are riding, a good idea is to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for better grip. Slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When another rider is passing you, why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: It stops the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to complete the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous. It may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What mistake do most riders make in crashes?

options.text: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
They brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.
They only use the front brake.
They only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: Which statement about helmets is correct?

options.text: It should meet U.S. DOT standards.
It should have no visible damage.
It can be reused after a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be reused after a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage. A helmet worn during a crash must be replaced.

questions.question: If you lock your rear wheel while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane often has an oily strip. When is this area safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Usually, unless the road is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this area usually provides enough traction for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Which item is NOT required for a street-legal motorcycle?

options.text: A seat that fits two people.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat that fits two people.
questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have at least a headlight, taillight, and brake light; front and rear brakes; turn signals; a horn; and two mirrors.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
The best position depends on your riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on your riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position based on your current riding conditions. This helps you stay safe and be visible to other drivers.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, what happens to your front tire's grip?

options.text: You can brake harder with the front brake.
You should reduce front brake pressure.
You can brake harder with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can brake harder with the front brake.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, your front wheel has more grip. This means you can apply the front brake with more force.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This puts them near the front of the group, allowing more experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What should you do if a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare it away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane if an animal is in your path. Swerving into traffic to avoid a small animal can cause a crash with another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than risking a collision with another car.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride when in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This allows experienced riders in the back to keep watch over them.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding. Bright red, orange, yellow, and green work best. Dark colors are harder for others to see.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane on a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side and can run off the road if you ride too far right. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may also leave the road if you get too close to the edge.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid blind spots and surface hazards. It should give you an escape route if danger appears, not block one.

questions.question: Proper clothing can protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury during a crash. It also protects you from heat, cold, debris, and hot motorcycle parts. It cannot protect you from other drivers' actions.

questions.question: What should you do with your head when riding through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider will slow down or stop. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.
